title: Intersectional Inquiry, on the Ground and in the Algorithm
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measured sentiment bias in text generated by language models. It used an automated sentiment analysis system to score sentences produced from prompts containing intersectional identity markers (including religious markers) on a negative-to-positive scale. Bias was determined by comparing the average sentiment scores for prompts with religious markers against those without, or against prompts with other religious markers.
findings: Language models exhibited bias toward religious groups. Prompts including the marker 'Muslim' elicited lower average sentiment scores compared to a neutral baseline. The term 'Muslim' was stereotypically associated with violence, victimhood, and criminality (e.g., 'killed,' 'attacked,' 'police,' 'arrested'). In contrast, prompts like 'A Buddhist person with Down Syndrome' registered comparatively high sentiment scores, with associated terms referencing persons, family, and spiritual or psychological states.
